summary_paragraph: A man with a history of nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, COPD, and cocaine abuse was admitted for acute chest pain and worsening shortness of breath following a crack cocaine binge. He presented with signs of volume overload and hypoxia. Evaluation showed no acute myocardial infarction but revealed demand ischemia and an acute exacerbation of chronic systolic heart failure. He was treated with IV furosemide, leading to resolution of edema and improved oxygenation. His diabetes became transiently harder to control due to stress and medication effects, requiring temporary insulin adjustment. An echocardiogram showed stable severely reduced ejection fraction with mild progression of left ventricular dilation. He was evaluated by social work and provided with mental health resources. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue cardiac and diabetic medications, monitor daily weights, restrict salt, and avoid substance use.
